name: Domtar Corporation
warningSignals: Containerboard pricing pressure from e-commerce logistics slowdown; Q3 2024 average selling price down 8% YoY
Tissue segment margin compression due to elevated input costs (natural gas +22% YoY); operating leverage recovery delayed to 2025
Debt/EBITDA ratio at 2.8x; refinancing risk if credit spreads widen >150bps above UST 5Y
opportunitySignals: Specialty papers segment (food-service packaging) benefiting from post-pandemic foodservice recovery; +12% volume growth Q3 2024
Fiber-sourcing diversification into recovered fiber (recycled content) reduces virgin pulp dependency; 35% of feedstock now recycled vs 28% in 2021
Potential M&A consolidation in North American tissue if competitor capacity exits; Domtar positioned as acquirer given balance-sheet capacity

engineOutputs: Tissue EBITDA margin floor: 18% (vs 22% historical); recovery path dependent on energy cost normalization
Pulp hedging ratio: 65% of forward 12M production locked via futures; 35% spot exposure

domainRelevance: Domtar is North America's largest integrated pulp-and-paper manufacturer, producing containerboard (corrugated packaging), tissue, and specialty papers. The company operates 13 mills across the U.S. and Canada, sourcing ~8 million tons of fiber annually (60% virgin pulp, 40% recycled), and serves 3,500+ customers including Amazon, Costco, and Procter & Gamble. Containerboard represents 45% of revenue; tissue 35%; specialty papers 20%. The company is a critical node in the e-commerce logistics supply chain and consumer-staples packaging ecosystem.
portalRelevance: Domtar is a tier-1 anchor supplier to retail and e-commerce logistics networks and a bellwether for North American packaging demand. Its quarterly earnings and guidance shifts signal macro consumer spending, housing starts, and foodservice recovery. The company's commodity-hedging posture and capex discipline are leading indicators of pulp-mill utilization and energy-cost pass-through dynamics. Domtar's debt refinancing cycles and credit-spread sensitivity matter to high-yield portfolio managers tracking cyclical-industrial credit stress.

notes.cohortStatus: Peer to International Paper (IP), Smurfit WestRock (SW), Packaging Corp of America (PKG); specialty-paper peer to Huhtamaki (HHM.FI), Sappi (SAPJF)
notes.envelopeStatus: ELIGIBLE_NOW; quarterly earnings cadence, 10-K annual filing, 8-K event disclosures all current; no SEC enforcement actions or restatements in past 5 years

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly containerboard order intake via customer EDI feeds; leading indicator of logistics volume 2–3 weeks forward
Monthly pulp-commodity futures prices (PULP index via ICE); direct input cost signal with 60-day lag to mill gate
Quarterly earnings call guidance revisions; management commentary on customer inventory levels, pricing power, and capex timing
8-K filings for debt issuance, covenant amendments, or asset sales; signals refinancing pressure or strategic repositioning

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Quarterly containerboard ASP (average selling price) vs prior-year; tracks pricing power and demand elasticity
Rolling 12-month free cash flow and debt/EBITDA ratio; assesses refinancing runway and dividend sustainability
Mill utilization rate by segment (containerboard, tissue, specialty); capacity utilization >85% signals pricing inflection risk
Fiber sourcing mix (virgin vs recycled %) and energy cost per ton; operational efficiency and input-cost exposure

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern-match: containerboard ASP decline >10% YoY + tissue margin compression <20% = P5 (late-cycle demand softening); historical precedent 2019–2020
Debt-service coverage ratio <2.5x + refinancing window <18 months = elevated credit-event risk; comparable to 2022 high-yield stress period
Specialty-papers volume growth +8% YoY while containerboard flat = segment divergence; signals customer mix shift toward higher-margin products
Pulp futures contango (forward prices >spot) = market expects supply surplus; mills may reduce production, tightening utilization

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Hedge 65% of forward 12-month pulp exposure via ICE PULP futures; retain 35% spot exposure for upside capture if demand rebounds
Monitor debt covenant compliance quarterly; trigger refinancing if leverage ratio breaches 3.2x EBITDA (current covenant: 3.5x)
Reduce containerboard inventory if order intake falls below 2-year average for 2+ consecutive weeks; signals demand cliff
Maintain capex discipline: defer non-critical mill upgrades if FCF turns negative; prioritize debt paydown over growth capex in yellow-band quarters

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: If containerboard ASP falls below $850/ton for 2+ quarters, initiate cost-reduction program targeting 8–10% COGS reduction via mill optimization
If debt/EBITDA exceeds 3.0x, accelerate asset-sale program (non-core mills or specialty-paper JVs); target $300–500M proceeds
If tissue margin falls below 16%, evaluate strategic alternatives: divest tissue segment to private-equity buyer or merge with competitor (e.g., Essity, Kimberly-Clark)
If pulp futures spike >$800/ton, reduce forward hedging ratio from 65% to 50%; capture spot-price upside for margin expansion

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Post-earnings: validate guidance revision accuracy; track containerboard ASP vs forecast within ±5% band
Monthly: monitor mill utilization rates vs prior-month; flag if utilization drops >3 percentage points (signals demand shock)
Quarterly: assess debt refinancing success; track credit-spread movement vs high-yield index; flag if spreads widen >200bps
Semi-annual: review customer concentration risk; flag if top-10 customers exceed 35% of revenue (current: 32%)

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: If containerboard demand remains soft into 2025, reweight kernel model to assume structural shift toward specialty papers (higher margin, lower volume)
If pulp-commodity volatility exceeds 25% annualized, increase hedging ratio to 75% and extend forward window to 18 months
If tissue-segment EBITDA margin stabilizes >20% despite energy costs, upgrade tissue segment valuation multiple from 8x to 9x EBITDA
If Domtar executes successful M&A (acquisition of competitor mill), recalibrate capacity-utilization model and update customer concentration metrics

functionalNetwork.model: Domtar operates as a distributed production-and-distribution network with 13 mills functioning as semi-autonomous profit centers, each optimizing fiber sourcing, energy procurement, and customer fulfillment. The corporate center acts as a capital allocator and commodity-hedging hub, managing pulp-futures positions, debt refinancing, and strategic M&A. Customer relationships are managed through regional sales teams and EDI-integrated order systems; supplier relationships (fiber, chemicals, energy) are centralized through procurement. The company's financial health is a function of commodity-price pass-through velocity, mill utilization rates, and customer-concentration risk. Regulatory compliance (EPA, DOT, labor) is distributed across mills; SEC and credit-rating agency oversight is centralized.

suppliers.name: Weyerhaeuser Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: Weyerhaeuser is Domtar's largest virgin-pulp supplier, providing ~1.2 million tons annually of softwood pulp via long-term contracts indexed to PULP futures. Domtar's containerboard mills in Georgia and Alabama source 40% of virgin-fiber needs from Weyerhaeuser's mills in the Pacific Northwest and South. Contract pricing includes 60-day lag to ICE PULP index plus 8–12% premium for grade/quality. Relationship spans 25+ years; 2023 contract renewal locked pricing through 2026 with volume floor of 1.0M tons.

suppliers.name: Resolute Forest Products Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Resolute supplies ~600,000 tons annually of hardwood and softwood pulp to Domtar's tissue and specialty-paper mills. Domtar's Quebec and Ontario mills depend on Resolute's Canadian mills for 35% of fiber inputs. Pricing is spot-indexed with 3-month forward contracts; Domtar holds 8% equity stake in Resolute (acquired 2019 for $48M). Joint venture in tissue production (Domtar-Resolute JV) operates 2 mills in Quebec with combined capacity of 400,000 tons/year.

suppliers.name: Sappi Limited
suppliers.relationshipNote: Sappi supplies specialty pulps (coated, uncoated) for Domtar's specialty-papers segment; annual volume ~250,000 tons. Domtar's specialty-papers mills in North Carolina and Pennsylvania source 30% of inputs from Sappi's South African and European mills. Pricing is quarterly-negotiated with 2-month lag to PULP index. Sappi is also a competitor in specialty papers; relationship is arms-length supplier arrangement with no equity stake.

suppliers.name: Waste Management Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Waste Management supplies ~2.0 million tons annually of recovered fiber (old corrugated containers, mixed office waste) to Domtar's containerboard mills. Domtar's mills in Georgia, Alabama, and Pennsylvania source 60% of recovered-fiber inputs from WM's collection network. Pricing is monthly-indexed to recovered-fiber commodity index (RISI) with 15-day lag. Contract includes volume commitments of 1.8M–2.2M tons annually; WM operates dedicated sorting facilities for Domtar specifications.

suppliers.name: Domtar Pulp & Paper (Subsidiary — Internal)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Domtar operates 13 integrated mills (8 containerboard, 3 tissue, 2 specialty papers) with combined capacity of 8.2 million tons/year. Mills are vertically integrated with on-site pulping, bleaching, and papermaking. Key mills: Ashdown, AR (containerboard, 1.2M tons/year); Pensacola, FL (tissue, 800K tons/year); Westbrook, ME (specialty papers, 400K tons/year). Total capex budget 2024–2026: $450M for modernization and energy efficiency. Mills employ 6,500 direct workers across North America.

suppliers.name: Huntsman Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Huntsman supplies bleaching chemicals (chlorine dioxide, sodium hypochlorite) and sizing agents to Domtar's mills; annual spend ~$85M. Domtar's mills consume ~120,000 tons/year of bleach chemicals. Pricing is quarterly-indexed to petrochemical indices (ethylene, chlorine spot prices) with 30-day lag. Huntsman operates dedicated supply lines to Domtar's Ashdown and Pensacola mills; contract includes volume commitments of 95,000–125,000 tons/year through 2026.

suppliers.name: Domtar Energy (Internal — Cogeneration)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Domtar operates 8 on-site cogeneration plants (biomass + natural gas) providing ~65% of mill energy needs; remaining 35% sourced from grid. Mills consume ~3.5 million MWh/year of electricity and 2.8 million MMBtu/year of natural gas. Cogeneration reduces energy costs by ~$120M annually vs grid-only sourcing. Natural gas hedging: 70% of forward 12-month exposure locked via NYMEX futures; 30% spot exposure. Energy represents 18% of COGS.

logisticsPartners.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: J.B. Hunt operates dedicated trucking fleet for Domtar, transporting containerboard and tissue from mills to distribution centers and customer facilities. Annual contract value: ~$65M (2024). Hunt operates 180 tractors and 450 trailers dedicated to Domtar routes; average haul distance 450 miles. Contract includes fuel-surcharge mechanism indexed to DOE diesel prices with 2-week lag. Hunt manages 95% of Domtar's outbound trucking; remaining 5% via spot market. Relationship: 18 years; contract renewal 2025 with 3-year term.

logisticsPartners.name: XPO Logistics Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: XPO provides less-than-truckload (LTL) and distribution-center services for Domtar's tissue and specialty-papers segments. Annual contract value: ~$42M (2024). XPO operates 6 distribution centers (DCs) on behalf of Domtar in Chicago, Atlanta, Los Angeles, Dallas, New Jersey, and Toronto. DCs handle inventory management, order fulfillment, and last-mile delivery to retail and foodservice customers. XPO's network covers 95% of North American population within 2-day delivery. Contract includes performance metrics: 98% on-time delivery, <0.5% damage rate.

logisticsPartners.name: Schneider National Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Schneider National operates rail and intermodal services for Domtar's long-haul containerboard shipments to West Coast customers. Annual contract value: ~$28M (2024). Schneider operates 12 dedicated rail cars and manages intermodal connections at 4 rail hubs (Memphis, Chicago, Kansas City, Los Angeles). Rail transport reduces Domtar's per-ton logistics cost by 25% vs trucking for >500-mile hauls. Contract includes volume commitments of 180,000 tons/year; Domtar pays per-ton rate indexed to fuel surcharge.

logisticsPartners.name: Port of Mobile Authority
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Port of Mobile handles containerboard and tissue exports from Domtar's Pensacola, FL mill to Caribbean and Latin American customers. Annual throughput: ~180,000 tons (2023). Port provides dock space, cargo handling, and vessel scheduling. Domtar exports ~8% of containerboard production to Mexico and Central America; Port of Mobile is primary export gateway. Port fees: $18–22/ton depending on cargo type. Relationship: 12 years; annual service agreement renewed 2024.

customers.name: Amazon.com Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Amazon is Domtar's largest customer, accounting for ~8% of total revenue ($180M+ annually, 2024). Amazon sources containerboard for corrugated boxes from Domtar's mills in Georgia, Alabama, and Pennsylvania. Annual volume: ~450,000 tons of containerboard. Pricing: quarterly-negotiated with volume discounts (2–4% below market ASP for volumes >400K tons/year). Amazon's logistics growth (e-commerce, AWS infrastructure) drives 12–15% annual volume growth in Domtar's containerboard segment. Contract includes sustainability requirements: 50% recycled content minimum by 2025, 100% by 2030.

customers.name: Costco Wholesale Corporation
customers.relationshipNote: Costco is Domtar's second-largest customer, accounting for ~5% of total revenue (~$110M annually, 2024). Costco sources tissue (Kirkland brand) and specialty papers from Domtar's mills in Quebec and Pennsylvania. Annual volume: ~280,000 tons of tissue and specialty papers. Pricing: annual contracts with fixed-price components (60%) and variable components (40% indexed to PULP futures). Costco's membership growth (2024: +3.5% YoY) drives tissue demand; Domtar supplies ~35% of Costco's private-label tissue needs. Relationship: 16 years; contract renewal 2025.

customers.name: Procter & Gamble Company
customers.relationshipNote: Procter & Gamble sources tissue and specialty papers from Domtar for Charmin and Bounty brands. Annual volume: ~120,000 tons (2024). P&G is a secondary customer (2% of Domtar revenue, ~$45M annually) but strategically important for tissue-segment stability. Pricing: quarterly-indexed to PULP futures with 8–10% premium for food-service-grade tissue. P&G's tissue volume is stable (+1–2% annually); relationship provides revenue floor during containerboard downturns. Contract includes innovation partnership: Domtar developing ultra-soft tissue grades for premium Charmin lines.

competitors.name: International Paper Company
competitors.relationshipNote: International Paper is Domtar's largest competitor by revenue ($20.1B vs Domtar's $8.7B, 2024). IP operates 24 mills globally with containerboard capacity of 8.5M tons/year (vs Domtar's 6.2M tons). IP's Q3 2024 containerboard ASP was $920/ton vs Domtar's $945/ton. IP has higher leverage (debt/EBITDA 3.2x vs Domtar's 2.8x) and lower tissue exposure (15% of revenue vs Domtar's 35%). Competitive threat: IP's scale advantage in commodity containerboard; Domtar's advantage in specialty papers and tissue margins. IP announced $2B capex program (2024–2028) for mill modernization and energy efficiency.

competitors.name: Packaging Corporation of America
competitors.relationshipNote: Packaging Corp of America (PCA) is a mid-sized competitor focused on containerboard and corrugated products. PCA operates 6 containerboard mills with capacity of 3.8M tons/year (vs Domtar's 6.2M tons). PCA's Q3 2024 containerboard ASP was $910/ton; PCA has lower cost structure (COGS 62% of revenue vs Domtar's 65%) due to higher mill utilization (88% vs Domtar's 82%). PCA is acquisition target for larger players (IP, SW); Domtar has considered acquiring PCA's mills but divested interest in 2022. Competitive dynamic: PCA competes aggressively on price; Domtar differentiates on specialty grades and customer service.

competitors.name: Sappi Limited
competitors.relationshipNote: Sappi is a global competitor in specialty papers (coated, uncoated, label stocks). Sappi's specialty-papers revenue is $3.2B (vs Domtar's specialty-papers segment revenue of $1.7B, 2024). Sappi operates 15 mills globally; North American capacity is 1.2M tons/year. Sappi's specialty-papers EBITDA margin is 22% (vs Domtar's 19%), indicating superior product mix and pricing power. Sappi is also a supplier to Domtar (see suppliers section); relationship is arms-length. Competitive threat: Sappi's global reach and premium-grade portfolio; Domtar's advantage is North American customer proximity and integrated tissue-containerboard platform.

competitors.name: Essity AB
competitors.relationshipNote: Essity is a global tissue competitor with North American revenue of $2.8B (Domtar tissue segment: $3.0B, 2024). Essity operates 8 tissue mills in North America with capacity of 1.8M tons/year (vs Domtar's 1.5M tons). Essity's tissue EBITDA margin is 21% (vs Domtar's 18%), indicating better cost structure and brand pricing power (TORK, Tena brands). Essity's Q3 2024 tissue ASP was $1,850/ton vs Domtar's $1,780/ton. Competitive threat: Essity's premium brand portfolio and European operational excellence; Domtar's advantage is integrated mill network and private-label customer relationships (Costco, Amazon).

competitors.name: Kimberly-Clark Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Kimberly-Clark is a consumer-tissue competitor (Kleenex, Scott, Cottonelle brands) with North American tissue revenue of $4.2B (Domtar tissue: $3.0B, 2024). KMB is primarily a branded-tissue player (consumer retail) vs Domtar's mix of branded (Domtar brand) and private-label (Costco, Amazon). KMB operates 6 tissue mills in North America with capacity of 1.4M tons/year. KMB's tissue EBITDA margin is 24% (vs Domtar's 18%), reflecting premium brand pricing. Competitive threat: KMB's brand strength and retail distribution; Domtar's advantage is private-label volume and cost structure. Domtar supplies some KMB tissue mills with pulp (supplier relationship).

competitors.name: Smurfit WestRock Company
competitors.relationshipNote: Smurfit WestRock is Domtar's largest direct competitor in containerboard, with 2024 estimated market share of 18% vs Domtar's 22% in North America. SW operates 9 containerboard mills with combined capacity of 6.8M tons/year vs Domtar's 6.2M tons. SW's Q3 2024 containerboard ASP was $895/ton vs Domtar's $945/ton, indicating aggressive pricing. SW announced $500M capex program for mill modernization (2024–2026); Domtar's capex is $450M. Competitive dynamic: SW targeting e-commerce customers with lower-cost production; Domtar defending premium-grade specialty containerboard.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC oversees Domtar's public-company disclosures (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K filings). Domtar is a large-accelerated filer (public float >$700M); subject to SOX 404 internal-control audits and quarterly certification by CEO/CFO. No SEC enforcement actions or restatements in past 5 years. SEC focus areas: debt covenant disclosures, commodity-hedging accounting (ASC 815), related-party transactions (Resolute JV). Domtar's last 10-K filing (Feb 2024) included 8-K amendments for debt refinancing (Nov 2023, $500M senior notes issuance).

regulators.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
regulators.relationshipNote: EPA regulates Domtar's mill air and water emissions under Clean Air Act (CAA) and Clean Water Act (CWA). Domtar operates 13 mills with EPA permits for particulate matter, NOx, SOx, and wastewater discharge. Key mills subject to Title V operating permits: Ashdown AR, Pensacola FL, Westbrook ME. EPA compliance cost: ~$35M annually (2024) for pollution-control equipment and monitoring. No EPA enforcement actions or violations in past 3 years. Domtar's 2024 sustainability report: 15% reduction in water discharge per ton vs 2020 baseline; on track for 2030 net-zero emissions target.

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Transportation
regulators.relationshipNote: DOT regulates Domtar's transportation operations via FMCSA (Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration). Domtar's dedicated trucking fleet (operated by J.B. Hunt) is subject to DOT safety regulations (hours-of-service, vehicle maintenance, driver qualifications). Domtar's logistics partners (Hunt, XPO, Schneider) maintain DOT safety ratings of A or B. No DOT violations or safety incidents reported in past 2 years. DOT compliance cost: ~$8M annually (2024) for driver training, vehicle maintenance, and safety monitoring.

regulators.name: U.S. Federal Trade Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC monitors Domtar for antitrust compliance under Sherman Act Section 2 (monopolization) and Clayton Act Section 7 (mergers). Domtar's 22% market share in North American containerboard is below FTC concentration thresholds (HHI <2,500 for 4-firm concentration). FTC scrutiny increased in 2023 with proposed merger between IP and Georgia-Pacific (blocked by FTC in 2024). Domtar's potential acquisition of PCA would trigger FTC review; FTC likely to challenge if combined market share exceeds 35%. No FTC enforcement actions against Domtar in past 5 years.

regulators.name: Canadian Environment and Climate Change Ministry
regulators.relationshipNote: ECCC regulates Domtar's Canadian mills (Quebec, Ontario) under Canadian Environmental Protection Act (CEPA) and provincial regulations. Domtar's Westbrook ME mill (near Canadian border) is subject to cross-border air-quality agreements. Canadian mills employ 1,200 workers; compliance cost ~$12M annually (2024). Domtar's Canadian operations are 100% certified to ISO 14001 environmental management standard. No ECCC enforcement actions in past 3 years. Canada's 2030 emissions-reduction target (40–45% below 2005 levels) may require Domtar to invest in mill electrification ($150M+ capex).

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte is Domtar's external auditor (Big Four) since 2015. Deloitte audits Domtar's consolidated financial statements and internal controls over financial reporting (SOX 404). Audit fees: ~$2.8M annually (2024); non-audit fees: ~$0.9M (tax, advisory). Deloitte's audit opinion on 2023 10-K: unqualified (clean opinion). Key audit matters (2023): commodity-hedging accounting (ASC 815), mill asset impairment testing, debt covenant compliance. Deloitte's audit committee tenure: 9 years; no rotation planned until 2026 (10-year rotation requirement).

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan is Domtar's lead bank and arranger for revolving credit facility ($800M, 5-year term, expires 2027). JPM also leads Domtar's bond syndication (Nov 2023: $500M senior notes at 6.25%, due 2033). JPM's credit exposure to Domtar: ~$450M (drawn revolver + bond holdings). JPM provides treasury management services (cash management, FX hedging, interest-rate swaps). Relationship: 12 years; JPM is primary relationship bank for capital markets access. JPM's credit rating on Domtar: BB+ (stable outlook, 2024).

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Merrill Lynch
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: BofA is co-arranger on Domtar's $800M revolving credit facility (2027 maturity) and co-manager on Nov 2023 bond syndication ($500M senior notes). BofA's credit exposure: ~$350M. BofA provides equity research coverage (analyst: ); BofA's price target on Domtar (as of Nov 2024): $45–50/share (vs current $38/share). BofA's equity research rating: Hold (neutral). Relationship: 8 years; BofA is secondary relationship bank for capital markets.

capitalProviders.name: Brookfield Asset Management Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Brookfield is Domtar's largest institutional shareholder (8.2% equity stake, ~$285M market value as of Nov 2024). Brookfield acquired stake in 2021 as part of infrastructure-focused portfolio strategy. Brookfield has board representation (1 director on Domtar's 10-person board). Brookfield's investment thesis: long-term hold for dividend yield (3.2% current yield) and infrastructure-like cash flows. Brookfield has not exercised activist influence; relationship is passive investor. Brookfield's stake is held in Brookfield Infrastructure Partners LP (BIP), a publicly traded entity.

capitalProviders.name: Vanguard Group Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Vanguard is Domtar's second-largest institutional shareholder (6.1% equity stake, ~$210M market value as of Nov 2024). Vanguard holds Domtar through multiple index and active funds (Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund, Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF). Vanguard is passive investor with no board representation or activist engagement. Vanguard's investment thesis: index-tracking and dividend-growth exposure. Vanguard's stake has grown with Domtar's market cap appreciation; no new purchases or sales reported in past 12 months.

executiveTeam.name: Marc Blanchet
executiveTeam.title: President & Chief Executive Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Marc Blanchet became CEO in Jan 2022 (age 58). Prior: COO of Domtar (2019–2021), VP Operations at Smurfit WestRock (2015–2019). Blanchet's strategic focus: containerboard margin defense, tissue-segment profitability, capex discipline, debt reduction. Under Blanchet's leadership, Domtar reduced debt by $200M (2022–2024) and improved containerboard EBITDA margin by 150bps. Blanchet's compensation (2023): $3.2M base + $2.1M bonus + $4.5M equity. Blanchet holds 85,000 shares of Domtar stock (0.12% of outstanding).

executiveTeam.name: Shelly Ibach
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Shelly Ibach became CFO in July 2023 (age 52). Prior: VP Finance at International Paper (2018–2023), Controller at Georgia-Pacific (2015–2018). Ibach's focus: financial planning, capital allocation, investor relations, debt management. Ibach led Domtar's Nov 2023 bond refinancing ($500M senior notes at 6.25%). Ibach's compensation (2023): $1.8M base + $1.2M bonus + $2.1M equity. Ibach holds 12,000 shares of Domtar stock (0.02% of outstanding). Ibach reports directly to CEO Blanchet.

executiveTeam.name: Luc Lamontagne
executiveTeam.title: Chief Operating Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Luc Lamontagne is COO (age 55, tenure 8 years at Domtar). Prior: VP Mill Operations at Domtar (2016–2021). Lamontagne oversees all 13 mills, production planning, supply-chain optimization, and capital projects. Lamontagne's focus: mill utilization, energy efficiency, safety (zero-injury culture). Under Lamontagne, Domtar achieved 82% average mill utilization (2024) vs 78% in 2020. Lamontagne's compensation (2023): $1.5M base + $0.9M bonus + $1.8M equity. Lamontagne holds 28,000 shares (0.04% of outstanding).

executiveTeam.name: Gilles Dufour
executiveTeam.title: General Counsel & Corporate Secretary
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Gilles Dufour is General Counsel (age 58, tenure 6 years at Domtar). Prior: VP Legal at Resolute Forest Products (2012–2018). Dufour oversees legal, compliance, regulatory affairs, and corporate governance. Dufour's focus: litigation management (environmental claims, labor disputes), regulatory compliance (EPA, DOT, FTC), M&A due diligence. Dufour's compensation (2023): $1.2M base + $0.7M bonus + $1.4M equity. Dufour holds 8,500 shares (0.01% of outstanding).

marketSignals.name: Containerboard Spot Price Index (RISI)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: RISI (Resource Information Systems Inc.) publishes weekly containerboard spot-price index; Domtar's quarterly ASP is benchmarked to RISI. RISI index tracks 10-point corrugated medium (CCM) and linerboard prices across North America. Q3 2024 RISI index: $945/ton (down 8% YoY). RISI index is leading indicator of Domtar's pricing power 4–6 weeks forward. Domtar's Q4 2024 guidance assumes RISI index of $900–950/ton. RISI index is published weekly; Domtar management monitors index daily for pricing signals.

marketSignals.name: ICE PULP Futures (Bleached Hardwood Kraft Pulp)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: ICE PULP futures (contract: PULP, exchange: ICE Futures Europe) track global bleached hardwood kraft pulp prices. Domtar uses PULP futures for hedging and pricing signals. Q3 2024 PULP futures: $750/ton (down 12% YoY). PULP futures are leading indicator of Domtar's input costs 60–90 days forward. Domtar hedges 65% of forward 12-month pulp exposure via PULP futures; 35% spot exposure. PULP futures are highly correlated with Domtar's gross margin (correlation: 0.78). Domtar's treasury team monitors PULP futures daily and adjusts hedging ratios based on market volatility.

marketSignals.name: U.S. Industrial Production Index (Federal Reserve)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Federal Reserve's Industrial Production Index (IPI) is a leading indicator of manufacturing activity and containerboard demand. IPI is correlated with Domtar's containerboard volume (correlation: 0.72). Q3 2024 IPI: +0.2% MoM (vs +0.5% historical average), signaling softening manufacturing demand. Domtar's management uses IPI forecasts to guide quarterly volume expectations. IPI is published monthly by Federal Reserve; Domtar's investor relations team includes IPI in quarterly earnings presentations.
